_why: Every modification this build makes to the PREBUILT ciel PDK volume, declared.
The Dockerfile asserts which open_pdks commit the volume was cut from by
resolving /foss/pdks/<fam> and requiring the sha in the resolved PATH. That
assertion is about PROVENANCE and is blind to CONTENT: a step that rewrites a
file inside the resolved tree leaves the path alone, so the assertion keeps
passing while the sentence it stands for stops being true.
tools/pdk/pdk_local_mods.py digests the volume before the first local step and
again after the last, and requires every measured difference to be covered by
an entry below. Adding a patch step without adding an entry FAILS THE BUILD
naming the undeclared files -- declaring is not something anyone has to
remember, it is the only way to get a green build. The expect_* counts fail in
both directions, so an entry cannot outlive the step it describes either.
Paths are relative to 'root'. `*` matches one path segment, `**` any depth --
the version segment is a `*` on purpose, so the sha lives in exactly one place
(the Dockerfile ARG) and this file does not have to be advanced with it.

modifications.what: sky130 HD and HVL tech LEFs: the five M4M5 vias carried a met5 patch of 1.42um on a layer whose own declared WIDTH is 1.6um, so a route terminating on one reports m5.1. The patch is grown to the layer's own minimum and the matching VIARULE GENERATE enclosure from 0.31 to 0.40. Upstream bytes, not ciel's; the volume is the only place that owns them.
modifications.scope_note: met5 only. The same contradiction exists on gf180's Metal2/Metal3/Metal5 (8 vias) on far denser layers whose DRC consequences have NOT been measured. Those files are deliberately absent from 'paths', so sweeping them in would fail this check rather than ride along.

modifications.issue: no tracker issue; docs/DEFECT_gf180mcu_pl8_poly_dummy_density.md — fixed UPSTREAM at globalfoundries-pdk-libs-gf180mcu_fd_pv 2404d27b583b (2026-07-04), which this prebuilt volume predates
modifications.what: gf180mcuD KLayout deck: PL.8 (poly2 density) counted layer 30/0 alone while the same PDK's tech/scripts/fill_poly2.rb writes its dummy poly on 30/4, so a die meeting the 14% floor WITH the fill this PDK generated was reported as violating it. The metal rules in the same file already union metal_drawn + metal_dummy. A derived layer :poly2_result = :poly2 + :poly2_dummy is registered in generic_layers.rb and PL.8 reads it. :poly2 itself is NOT redefined: DPF.5 is poly2_dummy.separation(poly2, 5um) and device extraction is poly2.and(comp), so the union arrives under a new name whose only consumer is the density rule.
modifications.scope_note: PL.8 only. Upstream's own fix (2404d27b583b) instead RENAMES 30/0 to :poly2_drawn and gives the union the name :poly2, which also hands the union to every rule that still says bare poly2 -- geom.rb's off-grid check, guard_ring.rb and others -- across 28 files. Those verdict changes are NOT measured here, so they are left to advancing the PDK volume rather than hand-ported into a binary artefact. The anchors are exact whole lines and the step declares --expect 2, so on a volume that already carries the upstream fix this step FAILS the build instead of applying somewhere else.

modifications.what: gf180mcuD klayout tech: the volume ships libs.tech/klayout/tech/scripts/sealring.py, whose first act is to put libs.tech/klayout/tech/pymacros on sys.path and do `from sealring_cells import gf180mcu_sealring` -- and that package is not in the volume, so the script prints "Error: Couldn't load the seal ring library." and exits 0. No ring is drawn and the die reaches tapeout_precheck unsealed, which is what turned General.SealRing from NOT_DETERMINED into FAIL. This step installs the four-file package from the SAME upstream commit whose copy of scripts/sealring.py is byte-identical to the one the volume already carries (fossi-foundation/globalfoundries-pdk-libs-gf180mcu_fd_pr e11a8c98dfc9, sha256 84cfcb8e2d5cacb018af11856fe8df07f77f10a5b27a476247d5e2599f800ece); see tools/pdk/sealring_cells/PROVENANCE.md.
modifications.scope_note: gf180mcuD only, and ADDITIVE only: four .py files into a directory that does not exist in the delivered volume. Nothing upstream delivered is modified, hence expect_modified 0. The step refuses to run if the destination already exists, so on a volume that grows its own copy this FAILS the build rather than silently overwriting it. The two ihp families ALSO cannot generate a seal ring in this image, for an unrelated reason this entry deliberately does NOT sweep in: their scripts use a registered KLayout library (SG13_dev) which never registers because sg13g2_pycell_lib needs a 'cni' module absent from the image. Fixing that is a different change with a different blast radius; pdk_sealring_check.py reports it rather than hiding it.
